title: What If Every Blade of Grass Vanished Tomorrow?
subject: grass field

scenes.text: What if every blade of grass vanished tomorrow? The lawn is the smallest loss.
Grasslands cover about 40 percent of the land on Earth, outside Greenland and Antarctica.
Cattle and sheep graze them, and herders in dry regions can depend on those animals for their whole living.
Then comes the plate. Wheat, rice and corn are all grasses, and together they supply about 51 percent of the world's calories.
Bread, rice, tortillas and cereal would go first. Half of what humanity eats would be gone.
Grass looks like nothing at all. It is holding up the dinner table.
